QB-101.why: Dale was laid off on 14 August and his coverage ended 31 August: a termination that caused a loss of coverage. Brindlemoor is employer and administrator and counts from the loss of coverage, so the notice is due by 14 October 2026 (31 August plus 44 days) (2590.606-4(b)(2)). It is one notice to Dale and Rina at 41 Alder Court

QB-104.why: Mireille resigned on 28 August and her coverage ended 31 August; the reason for a termination does not matter, so a quit has COBRA (54.4980B-4 Q&A-2). Due by 14 October 2026

QB-105.why: Anselm's hours fell to 24 on 1 September, under the plan's 30, and his coverage ended 30 September: a reduction of hours that caused a loss of coverage. Due by 13 November 2026 (30 September plus 44 days)

QB-106.why: Delphine is Anselm's spouse, but the plan has her at a different address (Pinecrest Lane, Millbrook; they live apart), so a notice to Anselm does not serve her (2590.606-4(e)(1)); she is owed her own, at her address, by 13 November 2026

QB-107.why: Gerald died on 3 September and Ilse's coverage ended 30 September: a death that caused a loss of coverage. Due by 13 November 2026; her maximum period is 36 months

QB-108.why: Cass's divorce was final on 20 July, her coverage ended 31 July and his letter reached HR on 28 September, inside 60 days of the latest of the dates (29 September). The administrator has 14 days from receiving it (2590.606-4(b)(1)): due by 12 October 2026, not 44 days from the divorce

QB-109.why: Wren turned 26 on 12 August and her coverage ended 31 August; Hollis's written notice reached HR on 30 September, inside 60 days. The administrator has 14 days from receiving it: due by 14 October 2026, at her own address in Coldwater

traps.QB-201: Corliss was terminated on 21 August but never enrolled in the plan: nothing was lost, so there is no qualifying event (54.4980B-4)
traps.QB-202: Yusra's hours fell to 32, over the plan's 30: she stays covered, so a reduction of hours without a loss of coverage is not a qualifying event
traps.QB-203: Nils reported his 1 June divorce on 14 September; the 60 days from the latest date ended 29 August, and the plan does not accept a later notice (2590.606-3)
traps.QB-204: Odile never told HR that her son turned 26: the administrator acts on the employee's notice (2590.606-3), and none was received
traps.QB-205: Marlon's election notice was mailed on 12 August, inside his window; a second one is a duplicate
traps.QB-207: Hester moved to Brindlemoor Logistics, which shares the plan: her coverage is unchanged
traps.QB-208: Vernon's unpaid leave leaves his coverage as it was: no loss of coverage
traps.QB-209: Walt's Medicare entitlement did not end his coverage under the plan: it is a qualifying event only if it causes a loss of coverage
traps.QB-011: Ines Calder's notice was mailed on 6 July for an event in the second quarter: not this quarter's, and already sent

QB-102.why: Rina is Dale's spouse at the same address; the one notice to Dale and Rina serves both (2590.606-4(e)(1)). A separate notice is allowed but not needed

QB-103.why: Theo is Dale's child at the same address; the one notice to Dale serves him (2590.606-4(e)(2)). A separate notice is allowed but not needed

traps.M-4: Accepting a vendor's offer to send notices for a fee commits the company to its terms and hands the notices to a vendor; the notices are the plan administrator's to send
traps.M-5: The broker's line is wrong (a quit has COBRA when it causes a loss of coverage), and a reply that agrees with it acts on it
